domain: health-system operations - NHS emergency care four-hour performance prediction (UK public-service performance panel)
prediction_question: For an NHS England provider operating a consultant-led (Type 1) A&E department, will the percentage of its Type 1 attendances admitted, transferred or discharged within 4 hours of arrival decline in month M+1 relative to month M, given that provider's monthly A&E series (attendances by department type and booked-appointment status, over-4-hour counts, waits from decision-to-admit, emergency admissions) for all months through M, plus calendar month? A relative month-over-month change is used instead of a fixed standard threshold because the fixed thresholds measured near-uniform positive rates in recent years (see measurements).
prediction_time: End of month M, when month M's monthly CSV is published (measured: the September 2026 monthly CSV was already downloadable on 2026-10-21, i.e. a ~3 week publication lag). Every feature is derived from provider months <= M; the label is month M+1's within-4-hour rate versus month M's, and month M+1's row is published about a month after the prediction is made.
target_definition: Binary, computed from the source row of month M+1: within4h_rate(M+1) < within4h_rate(M), where within4h_rate(Y) = 1 - Attendances over 4hrs Type 1 / A&E attendances Type 1 for the provider in month Y. Unit: proportion of Type 1 attendances within 4 hours. Label source columns: month M+1's 'A&E attendances Type 1' and 'Attendances over 4hrs Type 1' (recorded in label_source_columns; excluded from shipped columns). Volume gate: provider-month excluded unless Type 1 attendances >= 100 in both M and M+1 (measured: leaves 124 providers with >= 24 such months).

sources.name: NHS England - A&E Attendances and Emergency Admissions, statistical work area (monthly provider-level CSVs)
sources.api: per-financial-year sub-pages (2018-19 through 2026-27) each link 12 monthly provider-level CSVs (about 30 KB each, 21 columns: Period, Org Code, Parent Org, Org name, attendances by department type incl. booked, attendances over 4hrs by department type, DTA waits 4-12h/12+h, emergency admissions); pre-2018-19 months are XLS-only; the main page also carries a cumulative 'Monthly-AE-Time-Series' XLS (all months in one file) for use on a worker
sources.license: Open Government Licence v3.0 - stated in the work-area page footer, linking to https://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/doc/open-government-licence/version/3/ (Crown copyright)
sources.access: anonymous HTTPS, no key. Measured 2026-10-21: 102 monthly CSVs (2018-04 through 2026-09) = 3,115,779 bytes fetched in 1.2 s total from the coordinator; year pages are ~71-81 KB each and 11 were read to enumerate the CSV URLs

sources.name: NHS England - monthly statistical commentary PDF (publisher's own summary product, used as cross-check)
sources.license: Open Government Licence v3.0 (same standing terms as the statistics pages)
sources.access: measured 2026-10-21 via web search snippet: '61.1% of patients were admitted, transferred or discharged within 4 hours in Type 1 A&E Departments in August 2026 compared to 61.7% in July 2026' - cross-check against the panel's own 60.9% for 2026-08 (difference consistent with revised-vs-provisional publication states)

license_evidence.note: Measured 2026-10-21 from https://www.england.nhs.uk/statistics/statistical-work-areas/ae-waiting-times-and-activity/: the page footer carries a menu item 'Open Government Licence v3.0' linking to https://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/doc/open-government-licence/version/3/. NHS England statistics content is published under OGL v3 unless otherwise stated; OGL v3 permits commercial and non-commercial reuse and redistribution with attribution. Third-party reusers (e.g. github.com/rajatgaur505/nhs-ae-performance-analysis) state the same basis: 'publicly available NHS England data (Open Government Licence)'.

split_strategy: Temporal, on the target month M+1, windows computed from the measured panel (97 provider-months per provider, 2018-04..2026-09): train targets 2019-01..2022-12 = 3,714 provider-months (2,098 positives, 56.5%); eval targets 2023-01..2024-12 = 2,449 (1,152 positives, 47.0%); holdout targets 2025-01..2026-09 = 2,538 (1,233 positives, 48.6%). Both classes present in every window. Positives cluster within providers (a declining provider tends to keep declining), so the conservative independent-unit count is the distinct positive providers per window: 110 (train) / 124 (eval) / 121 (holdout) of 124 providers. Features for the earliest train rows draw on 2018-04..2018-12 history. Rows are keyed (Org Code, target month); providers with <100 Type 1 attendances in either month are excluded by the volume gate.

measurements.panel_2026_10_21: Script .factory/ae_panel.py (this session, stdlib csv only): 102 monthly CSVs 2018-04..2026-09, 21,649 rows read, 20,497 (org, month) keys after revision dedup (keep max Type 1 attendances copy), 124 providers with Type 1 attendances >= 100 in >= 24 months -> 9,071 provider-months. Month coverage 97 months.
measurements.national_within4h_type1_by_year: computed from panel: 2020 85.1%, 2021 73.2%, 2022 62.4%, 2023 60.1%, 2024 58.6%, 2025 60.2%, 2026 YTD 61.0% - matches the publisher's own commentary (Aug 2026 Type 1 61.1%) and the NAO report's fiscal-year figures (Type 1 low 56.7% in 2022-23, 60.9% in 2025-26) within calendar/fiscal-year offsets.
measurements.label_base_rates_measured: m/m decline label: train 56.5% / eval 47.0% / holdout 48.6% (balanced). Fixed-threshold labels measured and REFUSED for this task: within4h < 95% (the constitutional standard) gives eval 97.1% / holdout 99.9% positive (uniform-class red flag); < 80% gives holdout 95.8%; < 74% gives holdout 90.8%. Base rate is non-stationary with the system's deterioration (documented property, not a construction fault): a fixed threshold that separates in 2019 does not separate in 2025.
measurements.cost_measured: 102 CSV GETs, 3,115,779 bytes, 1.2 s wall clock on the coordinator (1.9 GiB class host) + 11 year-page GETs (~80 KB each) to enumerate URLs. Full-history extension to 2015-06 requires the cumulative Monthly-AE-Time-Series .xls (440 KB) parsed on a worker (xlrd), or per-month XLS for 2015-16..2017-18.
measurements.revision_policy_measured: recent months are republished as '...revised...' CSVs on the same year page (e.g. Monthly-AE-March-2026-revised); the panel dedups by keeping the copy with the larger Type 1 attendances; construction must prefer the latest revised upload and record the policy.
measurements.known_event_note: December 2021 (Omicron) moves the national aggregate only slightly (65.6% vs 66.2% in Nov 2021, quick un-deduped national check) - winter pressure shows at provider grain, so it is not a usable national known-event fixture; the publisher-commentary cross-check above anchors the rate computation instead. The m/m-decline label has no external threshold, so the qualification known-event fixture requirement does not apply; seasonal structure (winter declines) is the headroom signal a competent model must capture.
measurements.no_cross_split_entities: org codes repeat across splits by design (same providers tracked over time) - the entity is the provider-month, not the provider; the gate's expected_duplicate_ids must not claim org codes as entity keys, and id columns for the runner are (Org Code, target month).

next_action: GO to construction (advancement session owns it). Construction step: on a worker, enumerate year pages and download the monthly CSVs (2018-04..present; optionally parse the cumulative XLS with xlrd to extend to 2015-06), build the provider-month panel keyed (Org Code, month) with revision dedup preferring latest upload, apply the Type 1 >= 100 volume gate, label each row m/m within-4h decline for month M+1, features strictly from months <= M (rate history and deltas, attendances by type, booked attendances, DTA waits, emergency admissions, calendar month, provider code declared high-cardinality), ship nothing from month M+1's row, freeze train 2019-01..2022-12 / eval 2023-01..2024-12 / holdout 2025-01..2026-09, run the qualification gate on the full artifact, and measure seasonal-naive baselines (e.g. predict decline iff November/December, predict persistence) against a competent model on eval before quoting headroom.

novelty_check.ours: the first scored, split, leak-gated provider-month formulation of NHS England four-hour A&E performance direction (m/m decline, Type 1 providers, 2018-2026, temporal train/eval/holdout windows with both classes measured in every window); no existing artifact ships this prediction task with splits and a scored contract
novelty_check.rule: A dataset that already exists in ML-ready form is not published. Mirroring is a failure mode, not a contribution.
